extracted.intended_audience: researchers, peer reviewers, and journal editors involved in academic peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative arguments about how academic peer review should be organized and conducted, focusing on the double-blind vs open/transparency debate and reviewer behavior. The page argues for openness, reviewer accountability, and preserving research context when evaluating papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and open accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocate transparency and open accountability in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues that revealing reviewers' identities and decisions will refocus attention on scientific merit, reduce editorial power disparities, and improve the fairness of the process. Transparency is presented as a preferred alternative to double-blind review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure of reviewers' decisions and reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly disclose which reviewers rejected which papers and their reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemire explicitly proposes that journals should disclose which reviewers rejected papers and show their reasoning so authors and the community can assess the basis for decisions; this is an operational recommendation for implementing transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer accountability (reveal reviewer identities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer identities should be revealed so authors can assess reviewer competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revealing identities increases accountability: reviewers who know they may be identified will write more carefully, avoid nastiness and reflexive rejection. 'Anonymity is not a free pass.' The implicit scoring note is that accountable reviewers produce higher-quality, less abusive reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on double-blind peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Double-blind review is ineffective and tends to produce harsher reviews; it does not significantly improve paper quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post cites research indicating double-blind review doesn't substantially improve outcomes and may make reviewers harsher ('It is easier to pull the trigger when the enemy wears a mask'). The recommendation is to favor transparency/accountability over double-blind systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of research context and author trajectory
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate papers in the context of a researcher's broader trajectory rather than treating papers as isolated artifacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemire argues that research papers are often only interesting within the context of an author's broader work; double-blind review that conceals authorship undermines this contextual evaluation. Review processes should allow consideration of author history and research program where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect fairness for outsiders (assess impact on non-academic researchers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review systems should be judged by how they affect researchers from outside academia; data show double-blind can lower acceptance rates for outsiders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post notes that double-blind has been shown to disadvantage outsiders (contrary to intended fairness goals). When designing review policies, measure and consider differential impacts on outsider communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct: civility and carefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should avoid nastiness and reflexive rejection; anonymity should not be treated as a license for poor conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers expect their identity may be revealed, they will write more carefully and avoid nastiness. This is a normative rule for reviewer behavior intended to improve review tone and constructiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce editorial power disparities through mutual transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Mutual transparency (reviewers identified; reviews disclosed) can reduce editorial power imbalances between authors and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post suggests that making review activity visible to the community shifts some power away from editors and creates a system where editor and reviewer decisions are more easily scrutinized, thereby promoting fairness and accountability.
